project.name: WTW Diffusion
project.description: A Visual Studio extension (VSIX) that detects data changes between a target SQL Server database and a shadow database, generates migration scripts, and automates deployment. Designed for use with SQL Server Data Projects (.sqlproj).

projects.name: data-foundry
projects.description: Visual Studio extension. Contains all VS SDK, DTE, and WPF UI code.
notes: Uses System.Data.SqlClient (not Microsoft.Data.SqlClient) in orchestrator for legacy compat.
AzureSqlAuthenticationProvider, SqlMigrationRepository, ChangeDetectionService, MigrationScriptManager, MigrationScriptGenerator are now resolved from WTW.Diffusion.Core via project reference.
All Core service types are fully qualified in SqlMigrationOrchestrator to avoid VS IDE ambiguity with deleted ghost files.
IMigrationExecutor in VSIX is a thin interface that extends WTW.Diffusion.Core.Services.Migration.IMigrationExecutor.
PowerShellScriptRunner stays in VSIX because System.Management.Automation is Windows-only SDK.

projects.name: WTW.Diffusion.Core
projects.description: Platform-independent business logic. No VS SDK, no DTE, no WPF dependencies. Enables future CLI/ADO pipeline tooling.

structure.Constants.cs: Global constants. NOTE: causes ambiguity with EnvDTE.Constants in VSIX — always use fully-qualified WTW.Diffusion.Core.Constants in VSIX files.

notes: DataTable.AsEnumerable() is not available in netstandard2.0 — use Rows.Cast<DataRow>() instead.
DataTableExtensions (AsEnumerable) requires System.Data.DataSetExtensions which is not available in netstandard2.0.
static using WTW.Diffusion.Core.Constants must NOT be used in VSIX files — conflicts with EnvDTE.Constants type.

futurePlanned.name: WTW.Diffusion.Cli
futurePlanned.purpose: Command-line tool for Azure DevOps pipeline integration

staysInVSIX: ActivityHistoryService (uses System.Windows.Application dispatcher and VS ThreadHelper)

bugsFixed.fix: QuoteSqlIdentifier/QuoteIdentifier now escapes ] by doubling it (]]) per SQL Server standard instead of throwing. ValidateIdentifier now strips brackets before regex validation.

bugsFixed.description: Case-sensitive GUID comparison for DTE folder detection
bugsFixed.fix: Use StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase when comparing vsProjectItemKindPhysicalFolder GUIDs.

shadowDatabase.description: A shadow database is created from all migration scripts and used as the baseline for change detection. Smart caching avoids recreation unless migration files change.
shadowDatabase.cacheMechanism: SHA256 hash of all .sql filenames + LastWriteTimeUtc ticks. Cached in-memory and persisted to shadow-cache.json.

dualExecutionMode.description: Operations can run via C# (direct SQL) or PowerShell (SqlMetadataAutomation.ps1). Toggled by DataFoundryOptions.UsePowerShellScript.

migrationLogTable.name: __MigrationLog
migrationLogTable.idFormat: GUID embedded in script as comment: -- <Migration ID="{guid}" />

trackedTables.editableVia: Tools > Options > WTW Diffusion > General > Tracked Tables

importantConventions: VSIX files must use WTW.Diffusion.Core.Constants.Folders.X and WTW.Diffusion.Core.Constants.Azure.X (fully qualified) — never bare 'Constants.' or 'Folders.' due to EnvDTE.Constants ambiguity.
VSIX files must use WTW.Diffusion.Core.Config.DataFoundryConfig and WTW.Diffusion.Core.Config.TableListConfig (fully qualified) — bare 'Config.' conflicts with VS tooling namespaces.
SqlMigrationOrchestrator field types and constructor instantiations use fully-qualified Core namespace paths to prevent IDE ghost-file ambiguity.
All SQL identifiers (database, table, column names) must be quoted via QuoteIdentifier/QuoteSqlIdentifier which escapes ] as ]] per SQL Server standard.
MigrationScriptGenerator.FormatSqlLiteral handles null, DBNull, DateTime, bool, byte[], string, Guid, IFormattable — string values escape single quotes by doubling them.
buildNotes: VSIX project must be built via Visual Studio — direct MSBuild.exe invocation fails with MC6000 (missing WindowsBase) due to WPF/WinFx targets requiring the correct 32/64-bit toolchain selection.
WTW.Diffusion.Core can be built with 'dotnet build' independently.
If CS2001 ghost errors appear for deleted VSIX service files, delete the obj\ folder and rebuild — these are stale IDE cache artifacts from open editor tabs.
If CS1503 type mismatch errors appear involving Core types in SqlMigrationOrchestrator, use fully-qualified type names — the VS resolver can confuse ghost in-memory files with Core types.
